target: ray flower (PO_0025331) absent (PATO_0000462); the red colour belongs to disk flower (PO_0025332)
fix: A qualified compound 'ray floret(s)' / 'disc floret(s)' maps to ray flower PO_0025331 / disk flower PO_0025332 before the head noun 'floret' (flower synonym) is tried; 'ray florets absent' never becomes flower absent.
reason: Kleinia heads are discoid: only the ray florets are absent, the disc florets are described.

target: scale leaf / cataphyll (PO_0006003) present at the shoot base (lower sheaths without blades); not leaf lamina absent
fix: 'lower [sheaths] bladeless' / 'bladeless sheaths' in Cyperaceae and Poaceae means the basal leaves are reduced to sheaths (cataphylls, PO_0006003). It is never a taxon-wide leaf lamina absent. If kept as an absence, it is limited to the lower leaves.
reason: Only the lowest sheaths lack blades; the blades of the other leaves are described as thin.

target: cauline leaf (PO_0000013) decreased amount (PATO_0001997); basal leaves pinnate
fix: 'nearly/almost leafless' is a reduced amount, never absent. 'Leafless' said of a stem or scape refers to cauline leaves (PO_0000013), not to all leaves.
reason: Ivesia has pinnate basal leaves; the stems carry few or reduced leaves.

target: inflorescence axis (PO_0020122) glabrous (PATO_0000453); 'stemless' stays stem absent / acaulescent
fix: 'axes' / 'axis' inside an inflorescence description means the inflorescence axis (PO_0020122), not the stem.
reason: Tillandsia cyanea is stemless; the glabrous axes are those of the spike.

target: no annotation: the fruit is unknown (missing data), not absent; the 'lower (median) lobe' belongs to the perianth limb (PO_0009058), not the fruit
fix: 'X not seen' / 'X not known' / 'X unknown' records missing observation, never PATO_0000462 absent. A 'lobe' with no named part takes the part of the current sentence (perianth limb), not the last-mentioned organ.
reason: Capsules were not collected; the semicircular lobe is a perianth lobe in Aristolochia.

target: domatium (FLOPO_0986021) absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: 'domatia absent' maps to domatium FLOPO_0986021. The leaf blade is only where domatia would be, never the absent part.
reason: Lack of domatia does not mean lack of a leaf blade.

target: basal sterile florets (lower sterile florets) lack a palea; the fertile floret's palea (PO_0009038) is acuminate
fix: GrassBase 'Basal sterile florets ...; without significant palea' is limited to the sterile florets. It does not make palea absent for the taxon. Treat 'sterile floret(s)' as a member context.
reason: Oryza has reduced sterile lemmas without paleas below the fertile floret, which has a normal palea.

target: glume (PO_0009039) awnless (awn absent on the glume); the lemma awn (PO_0025349) is dorsal
fix: 'muticous' / 'awnless' takes the part in the sentence where it occurs (in GrassBase usually 'Glumes ... muticous'). It is never a taxon-wide awn absent.
reason: In Alopecurus the glumes are awnless and the lemma has a dorsal awn.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) absent on the leaf, i.e. leaf glabrous (PATO_0000453)
fix: A heading 'Hairs: absent' maps to trichome (PO_0000282) absent, or the parent part glabrous. It is never the parent part absent.
reason: The hairs are absent, not the leaf.

target: annulus of the perianth throat absent (no PO class; 'annulus' is a rejected generic bearer word); the limb colour belongs to perianth (PO_0009058), not corolla
fix: 'annulus absent' must not fall back to the enclosing organ. With no annulus class, drop it. In Aristolochia (one-whorled calyx-like perianth), 'limb' / 'tube' / 'utricle' map to perianth PO_0009058, not corolla.
reason: The ring at the perianth mouth is absent; the perianth itself is described.

target: scale leaf / cataphyll (PO_0006003) present (bladeless basal sheaths); leaf lamina glabrous stands
fix: As X02791: 'bladeless' after a sheath word means cataphylls (PO_0006003) or reduced basal leaves. It is never leaf lamina absent for the taxon.
reason: Carex pellita has bladeless basal sheaths and glabrous blades on the other leaves.

target: caudex absent (no separate PO class; caudex is only a synonym of stem PO_0009047): do not annotate as stem absent
fix: In absence statements, 'caudex' must not resolve through the stem synonym. Drop it, or map it to a dedicated caudex (woody stem base) class once one exists.
reason: The plant lacks a woody caudex, but its flowering stems exist and are solid.

target: axillary leaf fascicles (leaves of axillary short shoots) absent; no plain-leaf absence. Also the present annotation reverses a negation: 'margins not thickened' is leaf margin (PO_0020128) not thickened, not leaf increased thickness
fix: 'axillary leaves absent' (Caryophyllaceae) means no secondary leaf fascicles in the axils, never leaf absent. 'not thickened' must be kept as a negated quality, not read as thickened.
reason: The plant has leaves; only the axillary fascicles are lacking.

target: phyllode leaf (PO_0025335) absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: 'phyllodia absent' maps to phyllode leaf PO_0025335, not leaf (Sarracenia: no flat, non-pitcher leaves).
reason: Only the phyllodes are absent; the pitchers (vascular leaves) are red-purple reticulate.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138), the marginal (intramarginal) vein, absent
fix: 'marginal vein absent' / 'intramarginal vein absent' maps to leaf lamina vein PO_0020138 absent. The leaf blade is the location, not the absent part.
reason: The blade is present and elliptic; only a marginal vein is lacking.

target: cauline leaf (PO_0000013) absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' maps to cauline leaf PO_0000013, never leaf. The qualifier must be kept when the head noun is a lexicon word.
reason: Basal leaves are present and fleshy; only stem leaves are lacking.

target: scale leaf / cataphyll (PO_0006003) present (basal bladeless sheaths); leaf lamina flat stands
fix: As X02791: 'bladeless sheaths' means cataphylls (PO_0006003), never leaf lamina absent. This is the error given as the example in docs/km-classification.md.
reason: The basal sheaths lack blades; the leaf blades are flat.

target: probably a leafless part of the stem (upper stem or synflorescence branches, branch PO_0025073), not leaf absent
fix: A bare 'leafless' takes the axis it follows ('stem leafless above', 'branches leafless'). Whole-plant leafless (FLOPO_0985035) only when the plant has no leaves at all.
reason: Middle stem leaves are described, so 'leafless' must apply to some part of the axis; the source text is needed to confirm which.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent and oral setae (trichome PO_0000282) absent; 'brown setose' belongs to the (culm) leaf sheath (PO_0020104), not stipule
fix: In Poaceae and bamboos, 'auricle(s)' maps to leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106, never stipule. 'oral setae' maps to trichome at the sheath mouth.
reason: Bamboos have no stipules; both statements were mapped to the wrong part.

target: scape / peduncle (PO_0009053) ebracteate; the involucral bracts (PO_0009045) of the capitulum are present
fix: 'ebracteate' after scape, peduncle or pedicel means no bracts along that axis. It must not become bract absent, which by is_a also rules out involucral bracts.
reason: Gerbera scapes lack bracts, but the head has phyllaries.

target: no annotation: flowers unknown (missing data)
fix: 'Flowers not known' / 'not seen' / 'unknown' is missing data, never flower absent.
reason: The species was described from fruiting material.

target: no annotation: flowers unknown (missing data)
fix: As X02810: 'not seen' is missing observation, never PATO_0000462.
reason: The panicles (in fruit) were seen; the flowers were not.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent and oral setae (trichome PO_0000282) absent; no present annotation
fix: In a coordinated subject 'X and Y absent', 'absent' applies to every conjunct. A statement whose predicate is 'absent' must never also yield a 'present' record.
reason: The same sentence produced both absent and present for the auricle: a polarity bug, not a botanical conflict.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent (probably on the culm sheath); 'margin white ciliate' belongs to a sheath or ligule margin, not stipule
fix: As X02808: bamboo 'auricles' maps to leaf sheath auricle, never stipule. Keep the culm-sheath vs leaf-sheath context, since auricles are often present on one and absent on the other.
reason: Bamboos have no stipules. The epithet 'auriculatum' suggests the auricles are absent only on one kind of sheath.

target: 'slightly unequal' belongs to the umbel rays (primary rays of the compound umbel), not bracts; involucral bracts absent stands
fix: In Apiaceae, a quality without a named part takes the part of its own semicolon-delimited clause ('Bracts absent; rays ..., slightly unequal'). Keep bract (involucre) and bracteole (involucel) apart, though PO lists bracteole as a bract synonym.
reason: In Apiaceae descriptions, 'unequal' usually describes the rays.

target: peduncle (PO_0009053) arachnose / white arachnoid-tomentose; peduncle not bracteate stands
fix: 'not bracteate' / 'ebracteate' marks the axis as bractless. A following quality with no named part takes that axis, not the bract that was just negated.
reason: Bracts that are stated to be absent cannot be tomentose; the hairs are on the peduncle or stem.

target: rosette leaf (PO_0000014), i.e. basal leaves, absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: 'basal leaves absent' maps to rosette leaf PO_0000014 absent, never leaf. 'cauline/basal/lower/upper leaves' qualifiers must restrict the bearer.
reason: The middle and upper stem leaves are present and sessile.

target: leaves clustered at the stem apex (stem leafless below); no leaf absence
fix: 'leafless except at X' / 'leafless below' describes where leaves sit along the stem. It is never an absence. The 'except' clause cancels the taxon-wide reading.
reason: The statement itself says leaves are present at the apex.

target: check the source: 'Petals absent' may be limited (in some flowers) or 'oblanceolate' may belong to another organ (sepals or leaves)
fix: Look for limiting context ('in some flowers', 'or absent', 'sometimes') before asserting petal absent. If none is found and petals are also described, report it as a source contradiction.
reason: Not decidable from the two snippets; in floras this species is usually described with petals.

target: stem / cauline leaf (PO_0000013) decreased amount (nearly leafless scape); the white scarious margin probably belongs to phyllaries (involucral bract PO_0009045)
fix: 'almost/nearly leafless' is a reduced amount and is never absent. A margin quality with no part takes the organ of its clause.
reason: Youngia has basal rosette leaves and nearly leafless stems; scarious white margins are typical of the outer phyllaries.
